expectations.text: The output is split into two or more fenced mermaid blocks (by phase or scenario), not one giant diagram
expectations.evidence: 4 blocks — but structured as one giant end-to-end overview plus 3 focused repeats, rather than a true split.

expectations.text: No single diagram exceeds roughly 25 messages
expectations.evidence: Diagram 1 ('End-to-end overview') has 56 message arrows with 12 participants and 3 levels of nesting — the wall-of-diagram the split was supposed to avoid.

expectations.text: Participant names/labels are consistent across the diagrams
expectations.evidence: Same aliases across all blocks (Ord, Pay, Rest, Cour, Notif, etc.).

expectations.text: Each diagram has its own heading and short introduction, and continuity between diagrams is made explicit
expectations.evidence: Headings exist but diagrams 2-4 have no introduction text and no continuity links ('continues from...'); the focused views silently duplicate the overview instead of chaining.

expectations.text: All described failure branches appear: payment declined -> order FAILED, restaurant reject -> refund + CANCELLED + customer notified, courier decline -> retry with next courier
expectations.evidence: All three present, including the cancellation push 'Order cancelled & refunded'; invented event names are disclosed in the assumptions section.

expectations.text: Only widely-supported (safe-core) mermaid syntax is used, since GitHub rendering was requested
